import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))

# Color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=df['sensor_type'].nunique())

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
for i, sensor in enumerate(df['sensor_type'].unique()):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, s=40)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Camera Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_prices = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", len(brand_prices))
bars = ax2.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Camera Price by Top 10 Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for bar, price in zip(bars, brand_prices.values):
    ax2.text(price + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, 
             f'${price:.0f}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Megapixels Evolution Over Model Years
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year')['megapixels'].agg(['mean', 'std']).reset_index()
ax3.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['mean'], 
         marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=6, color='#2ecc71')
ax3.fill_between(yearly_stats['model_year'], 
                  yearly_stats['mean'] - yearly_stats['std'],
                  yearly_stats['mean'] + yearly_stats['std'], 
                  alpha=0.3, color='#2ecc71')
ax3.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Megapixels Evolution Over Time\n(Mean ± Std Dev)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Body Type Distribution with 4K Video Capability
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax4, color=['#e74c3c', '#3498db'], edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax4.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Camera Body Types with 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='4K Video', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_xticklabels(ax4.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha='right')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Add percentage labels on bars
for container in ax4.containers:
    ax4.bar_label(container, fmt='%d', fontsize=8)

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Dataset Analysis (n=1000)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
